page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring dedicated AMD EPYC processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing it in the top 10% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory performance is a notable strength, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, supported by a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 131.64 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small language models, achieving 263.35 tokens per second, while medium-sized model inference and database operations perform at average levels.

Given its high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU and integrated 1600 GB NVMe storage, this instance offers a resource-dense profile for memory-intensive workloads without requiring expensive GPU accelerators. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, strong memory performance, and local NVMe storage makes this server highly suitable for memory-optimized databases, caching layers such as Redis, data processing pipelines, and web serving environments.
